title: Tensor inheritance of the single-complex base-change condition
statement: For a cartesian square of schemes X' \xrightarrow{g'} X and S' \xrightarrow{g} S, with f:X\to S and f':X'\to S' the vertical morphisms [def-pc-base-change], let K \in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X) [def-pc-derived-category] and let L(g')^*K \to K' be a map in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_{X'}). For x'\in X', put x=g'(x'), s'=f'(x') and s=f(x)=g(s'). If for every x' and i\in\mathbf Z the canonical map H^i(K_x\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_{S,s}}\mathcal O_{S',s'})\otimes_{\mathcal O_{X,x}\otimes_{\mathcal O_{S,s}}\mathcal O_{S',s'}}\mathcal O_{X',x'}\to H^i(K'_{x'}) is an isomorphism, then for every E \in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X), the induced map L(g')^*(E \otimes^L K) \to L(g')^*E \otimes^L K' has the same property: its corresponding canonical map at every x' and i is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Fix x' and write R = O_{S,s}, A = O_{X,x}, B = O_{S',s'}, and C = O_{X',x'}. The stalk of the map for E tensor^L K is obtained by first forming E_x tensor_A^L K_x, then tensoring over R with B and extending scalars to C.

source.place: Tag 0DJA, proof of part (1), local stalk computation

proof.text: By the transitivity of derived tensor products [lem-pc-derived-tensor-transitivity], the source and target of this stalk map identify with the complexes obtained by tensoring the assumed stalk map for $K_x\otimes^L_{R}B$ to $K'_{x'}$ by $E_x$. Since $C$ is a localization of $A\otimes_R B$ (stalk of $X'=X\times_S S'$), it is flat over $A\otimes_R B$, so $H^i(-)\otimes_{A\otimes_R B}C=H^i(-\otimes_{A\otimes_R B}C)$ (Tag 00HT); hence the hypothesis says that $(K_x\otimes^L_R B)\otimes_{A\otimes_R B}C\to K'_{x'}$ is a quasi-isomorphism, and the same identification applies to the source for $E\otimes^L K$. Tensoring an isomorphism by $E_x$ remains an isomorphism, so the induced map on every $H^i$ is an isomorphism. Since $x'$ and $i$ were arbitrary, the inherited stalkwise condition holds everywhere.
